content.comment_body: Hi everyone, I'm new to this forum and to working with [company_name] [product_name], so I appreciate your patience. My friend and I are creating a program for a school exercise with the [product_name] controller. We've successfully tested and downloaded smaller programs, but when we try to download our full program to the device, we get an error called "non invertible output" or something similar—the exact message escapes me. Oddly, the program works fine during simulation. Does anyone know what could be causing this error?

Hello, try pressing F2 and check what the status window reports. Often, the problem is some function blocks that aren't connected to a subsequent contact. To fix this, use the "open connector" to properly terminate the function block, then you should be able to download. Simulation in [product_name] software generally works, but downloading to the actual device might not without proper wiring.
When you mention 'open connector,' do you mean an open contact? I'm a bit confused.

Each block used must have its output connected either to another block, an output, or a marker. Similarly, each block should be wired on at least one input side too. If you can, please share your program so we can take a look.
I'll upload the program once my friend returns from work so you can review it and offer advice. Thank you!

In [product_name] software, just press F2. The status messages show up below the editor, and if any function block isn't wired properly, you'll see it listed. Connect any flagged blocks and then try downloading again.

Here's the program. It's simulating a fermentation process: a main bottle is filled with mixtures from two others, followed by mixing, then moving empty bottles along a conveyor to be filled from the main one, repeating the process. Sensors help control everything. I've attached the file—let me know if you need more details on the I/O.

I tested your program on a [product_no] device and didn't see any download errors from PC to the controller. Which version of the hardware are you using? Your program should work in version [version_no] and above for function block programming. Some device selections throw errors: The following devices cannot be used: [article_no].Standard: [Flag] May not be used [article_no].L: [Flag] May not be used [article_no].LB11: [Flag] May not be used [article_no].Standard: [Input inversion not supported] ...and so on. Hope this helps!
We're working with version [version_no], but I'm not clear on why the M1 flag isn't allowed and why certain inputs aren't supported.

Looks like you're using software version [version_no] ([latest update is available]). What I meant is the hardware version of your [product_name]. To find it, check the number below the ESC button—it's something like [article_no]; the last number shows the version.
I can check now, but judging from the [product_name] units, I'm almost certain it's [article_no].
Please reply when you get a chance.

Your program looks fine and should download without issues. Where did you get your software? [product_name] V[version_no] was never officially released by [company_name]. Consider getting the official [product_name] or updating through Help > Update Center.

As mentioned, I had V[version_no]. I followed your advice and went to Help > Update Center, and now updated to v[version_no]. I'll try downloading it to the device again and may even rewrite it in the latest version. Should I also try with V[version_no]? My friend also tried downloading the program with official [product_name] software V[version_no] from [company_name]'s site, if that helps.
I've confirmed the version is [article_no], and the error when hitting F2 is "inversion not supported."

Hello [user_name], your program was created in [product_name] software with the target device set as [version_no] (check the status in the bottom right corner). Always double-click this area to select your actual hardware before programming, as newer functions might not be supported on older devices—that's likely the issue here. The instruction tree modifies itself according to the selected device version. In your code, somewhere an input to a function block is set to invert (logical NOT) by a black dot. This optimization works only on [version_no] and above. Replace these with a conventional NOT block and reconnect the wires. If this is the only issue, you should be able to download to your [version_no] device.
I made some edits so now your program should be compatible with [version_no]. Test it and let us know if you need more help.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encountered errors when downloading complex programs from [product_name] software to [product_name] hardware, even though simulation worked correctly. The main issues stemmed from wiring requirements for function blocks and hardware-version-specific feature compatibility. Users often found error messages and device selection requirements confusing, especially when certain flags or input inversions could not be used on older hardware, making troubleshooting more difficult.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a smooth workflow from simulation to deployment and clear, helpful error messages to resolve wiring or compatibility problems. They expect the software to provide detailed information on hardware version limitations, and they hope for straightforward troubleshooting guidance.
